featured_reviews.name: Murtaza Anverali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kheema Pav Review: Heaven‑Level Street Fix

This is the version you tell people about: hot keema—fine‑grain mutton, tomatoes, green chili—heaped on a plate with butter‑licked pav maska toasted till the edges crunch. Special Chai arrives in a huge glass, milky‑sweet with ginger bite, just enough to cut the fat. You break pav, drag it through keema, sip chai, repeat. It’s messy, fast, and perfect at 8 am when the stall lights flick on. You really do have to eat it there to get the story. 10/10, no substitutes.

featured_reviews.name: Tomas Kramar
featured_reviews.review_text: Went here because it was recommended in the Dishoom book but felt very disappointed. Ordered bun maska with chai and we were served a stale crumbly brioche that the server picked up from a box, packaged in a plastic wrap. The bun looked like a burger bun and had little nibs of colorful jelly mixed in. The people around us were eating proper bun maskas with pav and it seemed to me that we have perhaps been served a bastardized version intentionally to cater to our foreign palates. I asked the waiter if we can get the same dish as the other guests were eating, but English was obviously a problem and we have just received the bill and the waiter cleaned the table. I hope this was just a misunderstanding, but if you are a western tourist, eat elsewhere.

featured_reviews.name: Shivesh Bhatt
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let's start with the 40 minute wait. When you're made to wait that long, you naturally expect something rewarding at the end of it...The ambience was good, and after waiting so long to get a table, we were genuinely happy to finally be seated. The place is moderately expensive, and honestly, nobody mind paying a premium if the experience justifies it. Unfortunately, the service here was pathetic

My friend asked for a bottle of water and specifically requested one at normal temperature. Even after more than 30 minutes, it didn't arrive. When it finally did, they brought chilled water instead. I understand weekends are busy and service may take longer than usual, but taking that much time for a simple bottle of water is ridiculous

Not wanting to waste any more time, we ordered Masala Papad. When it arrived, it had no sev on it. Upon asking, we were casually told that they didn't have available. At the prices you're charging, are customers supposed to simply accept a poorer experience without question?

Then came the next masterpiece. One of my friends ordered a Diet Coke. After waiting more than 10 minutes, the waiter brought a regular Coke. At that point, all of us started laughing because it had become almost comical. When we asked whether they even had Diet Coke, he confidently said they did. The problem was that he had already opened the regular can before asking to change it.

Unfortunately, the experience didn't stop there. We ordered Tandoori Rotis, and the first round arrived burnt to the point that they looked like coal. We told the waiter and politely requested that the next be made properly. The second round arrived looking exactly the same. When we pointed it out, the waiter simply replied, "Weekend hai sir, ho jata hai"

For God's sake, man, we're here to enjoy our weekend too. Why are you ruining the experience?

Throughout the evening, we kept laughing at all the things that kept going wrong because otherwise it would have been frustrating. But when the bill arrived, I genuinely felt compelled to write this review. I rarely leave negative reviews and have never written one this harsh before, but this experience left me with no choice :,)

featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located at Colaba Causeway, this mughlai place is a pretty old and one of the legendary eateries which the city has to offer

The place has a royal ambiance but i believe they are definitely in a need of upgrade now.. especially the upper floors. The service is good.. initially it took a while for them to serve us as there was a huge corporate group having their party but once they had their attention to us.. they made sure that we are served well!

We went there for lunch, we ordered:
1) Roomali Roti: The roti was literally soft like a cushion and melts in your mouth, this is one of the best Roomali roti I have ever had.

2) Chicken Bhuna: Made on tawa, this boneless chicken bhuna was actually delicious. Chicken cooked was soft and melting in my mouth whereas the masala had right amount of spices to it and wasn't spicy which was to my liking!

3) Chicken Tikka Biryani: Usually the highlight of the restaurant, but to my surprise the biryani was better than what I had 1.5 years ago as it seems their chef has changed. The last time when I had it, the chicken was really dry and had been marinated in red color.. though it was charred well but was too dry! Whereas this time the tikka was properly marinated and grilled to the right amount leaving the chicken juicy and tender. The quantity served was good too. The rice i believe could have been more fluffier.

4) Sweet Fresh lime soda: The lemon concentrate at the bottom mixed with sugar and added soda.. mixed well.. definitely was refreshing but i wish they could add the fresh lemon juice for better taste.

Overall, a good place to have your fulfilling dinner.. the place had originally introduced to me by my mother.. though it might have changed over the time but still manages to have the same pull!

I recently dined at Shamiana in the iconic Taj Mahal Palace, Mumbai.

The food quality was truly impressive. Each dish was well-prepared, flavorful, and beautifully presented. The menu offers a refined dining experience that lives up to the reputation of the Taj brand. The ambience of the restaurant is equally commendable — elegant, warm, and comfortable. The overall atmosphere makes it a wonderful place for both relaxed meals and special occasions.

However, the service experience was somewhat average and did not entirely match the standards one would expect from a luxury property. While the staff were polite, the food was simply placed on the table once it arrived, and we had to serve ourselves. This was a bit disappointing, especially considering the premium positioning of the restaurant. Even many smaller restaurants ensure proper table service, so naturally, expectations are higher at a place like this.

Overall, Shamiana excels in food quality and ambience, but there is room for improvement in service standards to make the dining experience truly exceptional and aligned with the prestige of the Taj Mahal Palace.

featured_reviews.review_text:
As a loyal Taj guest who has stayed at the Palace, Lands End, and Vikhroli, all exceptional experiences, my visit to Shamiana for my wife’s birthday was deeply disappointing.

It started before I even arrived. I called ahead and was told no reservation was needed, walk-ins were welcome. At the door, I was asked if I had a reservation. That contradiction set the tone for the evening.

The crowd inside felt nothing like the Taj experience I’ve come to expect. The carefully curated atmosphere that makes Taj properties special was completely missing.

Most telling was the food. 3 out of 5 dishes were below par in terms of taste, which is surprising at Taj and especially on a special occasion. The Taj name commands a premium, and guests pay it expecting a premium experience in return.

I’ve stayed at and recommended Taj properties for years because they’ve consistently delivered. Shamiana feels like it’s living off the brand’s legacy rather than earning it. I thought I won’t be alone. Searched on Reddit and found similar experiences. Somehow google’s 4.4 star rating was out of sync or it may would have degraded recently.

A birthday dinner deserves better. I hope the management takes this seriously, because guests who know what Taj is truly capable of will notice the gap

featured_reviews.review_text:
Pretty good place. Very affordable. Got a seating immediately for 2 people. They do want you to eat fast though. Not a place where you can just sit for an hour at all.

I got the
1)Mutton Dabba Gosht: succulent meat, creamy taste. Literally the best dabba gosht ive eaten yet. They didnt skim out on the serving. Enough for 1 person to be full. ₹290

2) Bagdadi Roti: Huge Khamiri roti a little burnt ends as well. Adds chariness to the muttons flavour. For ₹25 amazimg value.

3) Bagdadi Fried Chicken: Huge leg piece with the extended up thigh of the chicken. Huge piece, perfectly fried, felt like i was eating tandoori fried chicken. Would absolutely recommend for the price of ₹150.

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
World of Palates, just a few seconds from Marine Drive, is truly a hidden gem for vegetarians. Celebrating their 1st anniversary on 11th December, they’re offering a special grand menu along with exciting discounts throughout the week — the perfect time to visit. The ambience is warm, cosy and thoughtfully designed, with comfortable seating for both small gatherings and larger groups. The charming book-filled corners add a unique, aesthetic touch.

We visited during their Sunday brunch, and the spread was delightful — fresh loaf breads, hummus, tacos, vibrant salads and juicy fruits that instantly caught the eye. The mains were equally impressive, featuring creamy mac and cheese, sautéed veggies, paneer lababdar, dal tadka, biryani and noodles. The highlight was definitely the desserts, with their pancakes and waffles stealing the show. A must-visit for anyone who loves global flavours and comforting vegetarian food.

The ambience was another highlight. The place is peaceful, clean, and feels welcoming. They also have a nice variety of books you can pick up and read, which makes the whole experience even more relaxing if you like slow, cosy lunches. The service was polite and everything felt smooth and comfortable.

If you’re around Nariman Point and want a lunch that feels calming and genuinely enjoyable, this spot is definitely worth visiting. 🍽️✨

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
After a long and hectic day at work, our group decided to unwind and walked across from our Head Office to Worlds of Palate, a charming pure-vegetarian restaurant located right in the heart of Nariman Point. The place immediately gives a sense of calm — a cosy, tastefully done interior with soothing music and warm lighting that makes it perfect for relaxed conversations.

We ordered a spread that truly showcased the kitchen’s range: Veg Biryani, Pesto and Pesto Pizza, and Spaghetti Aglio Olio Pasta. Every dish arrived freshly prepared, beautifully plated, and perfectly balanced in flavour. The biryani was aromatic and not oily, the pizza had a crisp thin crust with a generous layer of pesto and cheese, and the pasta was cooked al dente with authentic Italian seasoning. It’s evident that the restaurant uses quality ingredients and pays attention to detail.

Service was prompt and courteous, with the staff checking in just at the right times — not intrusive, yet attentive. The portion sizes were satisfying, and prices felt reasonable for the location and ambience.

What stood out most was the peaceful atmosphere, quite unlike the busy office district around it. Worlds of Palate manages to create a small oasis of calm in the middle of Mumbai’s corporate hub — ideal for colleagues looking for a quiet dinner or even a quick team lunch.

Overall, it’s a must-visit vegetarian restaurant in Nariman Point for anyone who appreciates freshness, flavour, and a relaxed dining experience. We left refreshed, content, and sure that we'll return soon.

The Gujarati thali is highly recommended, and dishes like amras puri and mini masala pav are definitely worth trying. The food feels authentic, portions are good, and service is quick and efficient even during busy hours.

Considering the prime location, prices are quite reasonable and offer good value for money. Paid roadside parking is available, though finding parking can be difficult on weekends due to heavy rush.

Overall, a great place for family dining with tasty food, quick service, and a pleasant atmosphere. Definitely recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of South Indian food, this place needs to be on your radar immediately. We recently had an incredible meal here, and every single dish hit the mark!

🍽️ What We Relished:

Ragi Dosa: Crisp, wholesome, and absolutely delicious. A fantastic, healthy option that doesn't compromise on taste.

Idli & Vada Sambhar: The ultimate comfort food combo. The idlis were pillow-soft, the vadas were perfectly crunchy on the outside, and the sambhar was deeply flavorful.

Cheese, Corn & Capsicum Dosa: A brilliant fusion choice! It was loaded with cheese, sweet corn, and crunchy capsicum with just the right amount of a chilly kick.

The Chutneys: A special shoutout to the chutneys served with the meal—fresh, vibrant, and packed with authentic flavor. They elevated every bite!

🍦 The Grand Finale:

featured_reviews.review_text:

The quality and taste are consistently good, which makes this place stand out from many other options in the area.

What I liked the most was the overall dining experience. The seating space is spacious, clean, and comfortable, making it a great place to visit with family or friends. Even during busy hours, the staff manages everything very efficiently. The team is polite, attentive, and always ready to help with recommendations or quick service.

Another big plus is how fast the service is. Despite the crowd during peak times, the food was served surprisingly quickly without compromising on quality. It’s clear that they value customer experience and maintain good service standards.

Overall, this is definitely one of the best South Indian food places in the area. Great food, reasonable pricing, quick service, and a welcoming atmosphere — highly recommended and absolutely worth visiting!

featured_reviews.name: Sree
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best culinary experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. I stumbled upon this spot tucked into one of the city’s busiest, most crowded streets, and it was absolutely worth navigating the chaos to get there.

I ordered the pav bhaji and chole bhature, and both were outstanding. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced with that authentic street-style flavor, yet it felt clean and hygienic. The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene

The restaurant is located in the busy streets of Zaveri Bazaar (well known for 1993 Mumbai Blasts), so driving a private car is out of the question. Cabs are very difficult to get by.

featured_reviews.name: Kapil Jaiswal
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Folk at Kala Ghoda for an office team lunch, and since it was our first visit, we were quite curious to see what the place had to offer. Safe to say, it turned out to be a fantastic experience overall—great food, lively ambience, and genuinely good vibes that made the afternoon enjoyable for everyone.
The first thing you notice when you enter is the energy of the place. Folk has a very vibrant yet tasteful ambience. It carries a modern Indian aesthetic with a creative touch, and the overall vibe feels upbeat without being overwhelming. For a team lunch, this worked perfectly—it was lively enough to keep the mood energetic but still allowed easy conversations across the table. The seating was comfortable, and the layout gave enough space for groups to enjoy without feeling cramped.
Coming to the food, we ordered quite a variety, and every dish brought something unique to the table.
The Aloo Tikki Chaat was a great start—crispy tikki topped with tangy chutneys and curd, offering a perfect balance of sweet, spicy, and tangy flavours.
The Chicken Tikka was juicy and well-marinated, with a smoky flavour from the grill. The spices were balanced, making it a crowd-pleaser.
The Dahi Kabab was soft, creamy, and delicate. It had a melt-in-the-mouth texture with a mild flavour that stood out for its simplicity.
The Kokum Fish Fry (g-free) was fresh and flavourful. The kokum added a slight tanginess, enhancing the taste of the fish without overpowering it.
The Kasauli Butter Chicken was rich and comforting. The gravy was creamy with a hint of smokiness, and the chicken was tender and well-cooked.
The Konkani Chicken Sukka (g-free) had bold coastal flavours. It was slightly dry, well-spiced, and packed with aromatic notes of coconut and traditional masalas.
The Mutton Galouti Kebab was one of the highlights—extremely soft, finely minced, and full of flavour. It literally melted in the mouth.
The Konkani Green Veg was fresh and well-balanced. The green masala was flavourful without being too heavy, making it a good vegetarian option.
For beverages, we tried the Aam Panna (v, g-free), which was refreshing and tangy with a perfect balance of sweetness and spice—great for a daytime meal.
The Masala Chaas was light, cooling, and well seasoned, making it a perfect companion to the rich dishes we had ordered.
What stood out across all dishes was the consistency in taste and presentation. Nothing felt rushed or average—each dish had its own identity and was prepared with attention to detail.
Service was smooth and professional. The staff were attentive and courteous, ensuring that our large group was well managed without delays or confusion. They were available when needed but didn’t interrupt conversations, which added to the comfort of the experience.
Another big plus was the overall vibe of the place. Folk truly lives up to its name—it has a social, lively energy that makes you feel relaxed and engaged at the same time. It’s one of those places where the atmosphere itself adds to the experience, especially for group outings like ours.
Overall, Folk at Kala Ghoda delivered a memorable first visit. Great food, vibrant ambience, and positive energy made it an ideal choice for an office team lunch. It’s definitely a place I would recommend for group gatherings, casual celebrations, or even a relaxed outing with friends.
Looking forward to visiting again soon.

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. Service is quick, portions are satisfying, and the overall experience feels homely and consistent without being overpriced. featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Sarah Chamdawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an amazing authentic South Indian breakfast at Santosham! Ordered the Mysore sada dosa, which was crispy and spicy and delicious; the ghee podi idli was fluffy and you could really taste the shuddh ghee; the beetroot rawa dosa was soo crispy and had just the perfect little hint of beetroot flavour; the benne dosa was yum and perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside and served with the most decadent pure white butter! The filter coffees (both cold and hot) were also delicious with the perfect froth on top! We also enjoyed the rose milk with chia seeds. The tomato chutney, coconut chutney and sambhar served on the side were also great and proved the perfect accompaniments to the meal.
A special mention for the service which was top notch, thanks to Nasim and Uday who were very helpful and quick.
10/10 would recommend this place!

featured_reviews.review_text:
The Best Pure Veg Spot in Neelkanth Business Park!

Lark is my go-to spot whenever I’m at Neelkanth Business Park. It’s a perfect mix of great taste, hygiene, and a professional yet cozy vibe.

Here’s why it’s a must-visit:

Signature Dishes: You have to try the Pineapple Shira—it’s sweet, rich, and has real fruit bits. For snacks, the Lark Special Idli (loaded with dry fruits) and Idli Chilly Fry are absolutely delicious and perfectly spiced.

Multi-Cuisine Variety: Their menu is huge! From authentic South Indian breakfast to spicy Chinese and North Indian Sizzlers, everything is fresh and flavorful. The Kerala Appam with Stew is another hidden gem here.

Cleanliness & Ambience: The restaurant is very well-maintained. The washrooms are clean, and the seating is comfortable enough for a quick lunch or a long team dinner.

Budget-Friendly: Despite being in a premium business park, the prices are very reasonable for the quality and quantity they serve.

Convenience: Located on the ground floor, it’s super accessible for everyone working in the park or coming from Vidya Vihar station.

Verdict: 5/5 for service, taste, and cleanliness. Definitely the best pure veg option in the area!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a casual dinner with my brother yesterday and experienced one of the finest services ever. They offered complimentary bottled water and papad with green chutney as soon as we were seated. The food was delicious—highly recommend the Peri Peri Rice 😍, a must-try! What truly impressed us was their service: they provided a fresh complimentary water bottle whenever it was empty and cleaned the table immediately after it was cleared. Exceptional hospitality overall.

“Free packaged drinking water dena unki service aur customer care ka clear reflection hai.”

featured_reviews.name: Jignesh Chheda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Achija Hotel is one of the finest options for vegetarians, with one of the largest outlets, spread across two floors: ground and basement. However, reaching the location from the Western Express Highway can be a bit challenging due to the narrow road and the traffic in the area. It’s easy to get stuck in congestion. Thankfully, the hotel management was very understanding of our situation and allowed us to keep our reservation despite being late, without giving it to anyone else.

I highly recommend making a reservation, especially during weekends or if you're visiting with a large group, to avoid long waits. The food is flavorful, with a wide variety of options to choose from. If you're unsure about what to try, checking Google Maps reviews can be helpful.

Personally, I recommend trying the Pav Bhaji and any of the paneer dishes, which are excellent. For other suggestions, feel free to ask the staff, as they are very helpful and cooperative.

Firstly pav bhaji costed 270/- its actually very expensive. And i am ok paying so much for bhaji n 2 pav, but I expect cleanliness n hygiene from them. Its food n they have to be serious about it.
